text:
Alex Chen: Customer ACME (eu-west-1) reports a spike of 504s on streaming completions starting ~11:05 UTC. They provided a trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d and say it affects long-lived streams (~30s+).
Maya Patel: Seen a small uptick in 504s around that time in eu-west-1, +12% vs baseline. No deploys.
Luis Ortega: Can you paste the trace logs? envoy shows upstream reset before headers often: 
```
[2025-06-03T11:05:12Z] envoy upstream reset: connection failure, id=0x7f3a
upstream response: 0x0 - upstream response timed out
```
Karen Li: Customer repro steps: open streaming connection + send prompt that yields ~25s generation. They sent curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","stream":true,"prompt":"<long prompt>"}'
```
Alex Chen: Initial hypothesis: auth backend (billing/account service) had transient write tail latency -> auth cache miss -> gateway waits on authz -> stream idle -> upstream timeout. Correlation: our billing write latency spiked at same minute in telemetry.
Maya Patel: I see `auth-cache-miss` rate jumped in ingress metrics: `auth-cache.hits 98% -> 65%` and `upstream_504 0.02 -> 0.14`.
Luis Ortega: Can we try bypassing auth cache for this tenant as a quick probe? Or reduce gateway idle timeout for streaming? Both risky.
Karen Li: Customer asked for workaround. Suggested: shorten max_stream_idle to 45s and retry with smaller batch in request. They can test now.
ingress-bot: deploy:scaled-midfront-pool eu-west-1 +2 instances at 11:07 UTC (auto-scale).
Alex Chen: Action plan: (1) SRE to capture tcpdump on one edge instance serving trace-0a1b2c3d, (2) Eng to check billing KV write latencies and recent PRs, (3) Support to advise customer to try smaller prompt/chunking.
Luis Ortega: Captured tcpdump + envoy access log for trace attached: 
```
{"ts":"2025-06-03T11:05:12.123Z","method":"POST","path":"/v1/stream","status":504,"upstream_host":"10.2.5.12:8080","upstream_response_time_ms":30010}
```
Maya Patel: Upstream response time ~30s consistent with their long streams. Envoy times out after 30s waiting for upstream headers. That matches default `upstream_request_timeout`.
Alex Chen: Temporary mitigations applied: increased envoy upstream timeout to 40s for streaming route (edge rule change) and added a 2s retry on auth lookups. Rolling now.
Karen Li: Customer tested — their stream completed when we increased timeout but still saw higher latency. They've accepted temporary workaround. :thumbsup:
Luis Ortega: Root cause postmortem candidate: billing KV write TTL rotation caused brief auth cache misses across a subset of midfronts -> gateway blocked on auth handshake for long-lived streams -> envoy upstream timeout surfaced as 504s.
Maya Patel: Follow-ups: (a) add circuit-breaker around auth service to return cached token if backend slow, (b) add longer tail timeout for streaming endpoints, (c) run chaos test on auth KV to validate.
Alex Chen: Filing a follow-up ticket for eng/infra to harden: ENG-2534. Notifying product and SRE. Thanks all.
